commentary_segments.text: The most accurate way to convert a voltage into a current is the use of an opamp. The reference voltage is imposed across the resistor. The output current is exactly the same as the current through this resistor. The main error is caused by the offset of the opamp. The temperature coefficient is determined by the temperature coefficients of the bandgap reference and that of the resistor. One could be made to compensate the other, depending on the application.
